title: Palantir Stock (PLTR) Falls 1.6% After Q3 Results (Nov 3)
summary: Palantir (PLTR) closed at $175.40 on Nov 3, down 1.65%, as slowing contract value growth weighed on the stock after its Q3 2026 results.
body_markdown:
The decline ran against a firmer market. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.83% to 25,372.01 and the S&P 500 gained 0.36% to 7,568.92, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.38% to 51,786.72, leaving Palantir 2.48 percentage points behind the Nasdaq. Several software and AI names moved the other way:[Oracle (ORCL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/orcl/) climbed 5.85%,[Microsoft (MSFT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/msft/) added 2.74% and[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) gained 2.29%. The US 10-year Treasury yield rose 5.8 basis points to 4.95%.


At the close, Palantir stood 17.63% below its 52-week high of $212.94 and 64.90% above its 52-week low of $106.37.


## Why Palantir Stock Fell


According to[the company's official results release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001321655/000132165526000045/a2026q3ex991pressrelease.htm) , published on November 2, third-quarter revenue rose 96% year over year to $2.313 billion. U.S. commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million and passed U.S. government revenue, which rose 96% to $953 million, for the first time.


> "Our U.S. commercial revenue has surpassed our U.S. government revenue for the first time in our company's history." (Alex Karp, Palantir CEO, in the company's Q3 2026 release)


The weak spot in the[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) was new business. Total contract value came in at $2.918 billion, up 6% year over year, per the release, compared with 49% growth in the second quarter, as reported by[the Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/palantir-stock-buy-latest-earnings-225002962.html) . The Motley Fool's session recap added that remaining performance obligations held at $4.9 billion, unchanged from the second quarter, and wrote that "it's Palantir's future that Wall Street is concerned about today."


Palantir linked part of the slowdown to deal structure. Customers adopting its new Sovereign AI capabilities signed shorter-than-usual contracts, which the company's CFO said are expected to grow in size and duration, according to the Motley Fool.


## PLTR Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Raised outlook: Palantir lifted its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.530 billion to $8.534 billion and now expects U.S. commercial revenue above $3.559 billion, growth of at least 143%, according to the release.
- Profitability: the company reported diluted GAAP earnings per share of $0.44, an adjusted operating margin of 62% and a Rule of 40 score of 158%, per the release.
- Cash and backlog: cash, cash equivalents and U.S. government securities totaled $10.4 billion, and U.S. commercial remaining deal value rose 79% to $6.517 billion, per the release.


### Risks


- Contract momentum: total contract value growth slowed to 6% and remaining performance obligations stayed at $4.9 billion, which the Motley Fool said pointed to a possible future sales slowdown.
- Shorter deal terms: the shorter Sovereign AI contracts can reduce reported contract value even when customer spending rises, the Motley Fool noted.
- Valuation focus: the Motley Fool's session recap put the stock at about 86 times forward earnings and said valuation stayed in focus during the session.
